source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions (Good 2 Great podcast collaboration with Prof. Harsimran Sandhu)
summary: A full macro history-to-framework conversation on the Good 2 Great podcast with Prof. Harsimran Sandhu (ex-Standard Chartered leadership, now Professor of Finance & Associate Dean at IMT Ghaziabad, PhD IIM Indore). They trace Bretton Woods to the Nixon Shock to the petrodollar/Saudi pact as the story of how the dollar became dominant, and argue that grip is now loosening via BRICS payment systems and central banks buying gold as the one asset that can't be printed. On India vs China vs the US: China is his pick as the rising dominant player (manufacturing plus rare-earth mining plus fintech, with transparency the big caveat); India's vulnerability is energy dependence, its opportunity a focused manufacturing base in a few strategic industries — defense, high-quality agri, pharma. Investor framework: keep a core 60-70% in a diversified multi-cap/flexi-cap Nifty-500 portfolio that needs no tactical tinkering; tactical plays only on the side — defense 'looks attractive' as global spending rises, wait on energy stocks while oil stays elevated, and be cautious on highly leveraged/rate-sensitive companies as RBI may hike in 1-2 cycles. Valuation rule: price-to-free-cash-flow over P/E or P/B, and beware new-age names valued purely on 'growth value' with zero franchise or breakup value. Six macro indicators to watch: private capex, monsoon, Brent crude, fiscal deficit (~4.3-4.5% target), credit flow, and CPI/WPI inflation. No explicit calls in this one — no BUY/SELL/HOLD on any ticker.
